reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: Caused by HADHA variants affecting the alpha subunit of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein, which carries the long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity; the common c.1528G>C variant is characteristic
Distinctive complications not seen in most other oxidation defects are progressive pigmentary retinopathy and peripheral neuropathy
Carrying an affected fetus is strongly associated with maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy and HELLP syndrome
Newborn screening shows elevated long-chain hydroxyacylcarnitines, notably 3-hydroxytetradecanoylcarnitine (C16-OH) and related hydroxy species
Acute presentations include hypoketotic hypoglycaemia, cardiomyopathy, hepatic dysfunction and rhabdomyolysis, overlapping with generalised trifunctional protein deficiency
Management combines long-chain fat restriction with medium-chain triglyceride substitution, avoidance of fasting and an emergency regimen during illness
Regular ophthalmological surveillance is needed because retinopathy can progress despite metabolic control
reference.pathophysiology: The mitochondrial trifunctional protein is a membrane-bound complex that catalyses three sequential steps of long-chain fatty-acid beta-oxidation; isolated LCHAD deficiency reflects selective loss of the 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity of its alpha subunit. Blocked long-chain oxidation impairs energy supply to heart, muscle and liver during fasting and stress and prevents hepatic ketogenesis, while accumulation of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl metabolites is thought to be toxic and to underlie the retinopathy and neuropathy. Transplacental passage of these hydroxy intermediates from an affected fetus is implicated in the maternal liver disease of pregnancy.
additionalDifferentials: Generalised mitochondrial trifunctional protein deficiency (alpha and beta subunit involvement)
Carnitine palmitoyltransferase II and translocase deficiencies
Other causes of infantile cardiomyopathy or hepatopathy
Inherited retinal dystrophies and peripheral neuropathies of other cause
Sepsis or metabolic acidosis in a decompensating infant
additionalInvestigations: Plasma acylcarnitine profile showing raised long-chain hydroxyacylcarnitines (e.g. C16-OH, C18:1-OH)
Blood glucose, ketones, ammonia, lactate and liver function during illness
Ophthalmological assessment and electroretinography for retinopathy, and nerve conduction studies for neuropathy
HADHA molecular genetic testing to confirm the diagnosis
Echocardiography and creatine kinase during acute decompensation
redFlags: Maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy or HELLP syndrome prompting testing of the infant
Hypoketotic hypoglycaemia with encephalopathy or cardiomyopathy
Rhabdomyolysis with pigmenturia and acute kidney injury risk
Progressive visual loss or neuropathic symptoms indicating chronic complications
reference.prognosis: Early screen-detected diagnosis and dietary management improve survival and reduce acute crises, but retinopathy and neuropathy may progress over time, so long-term morbidity remains a concern even with good metabolic control.
pitfalls: Not testing the neonate after maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy or HELLP syndrome
Overlooking retinopathy or neuropathy because acute metabolic control appears adequate
Using unrestricted long-chain fat instead of medium-chain triglyceride substitution
Permitting fasting for procedures without a glucose-containing infusion
references: Scriver's OMMBID (Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease)
management: Base dietary treatment on long-chain fat restriction with medium-chain triglyceride substitution, frequent feeds, and complex carbohydrate to bypass the block in long-chain fat oxidation, with triheptanoin as an anaplerotic fat source in some
Strictly avoid fasting and implement an emergency regimen of high carbohydrate intake, with intravenous glucose during illness, to prevent catabolic decompensation
Supplement docosahexaenoic acid to slow the characteristic pigmentary retinopathy
Manage acute crises with intravenous dextrose and treatment of hypoketotic hypoglycaemia, rhabdomyolysis, and cardiomyopathy

Undertake surveillance with acylcarnitine profiles, growth and dietary review, echocardiography and creatine kinase, and ophthalmological (electroretinography) and nerve-conduction monitoring for retinopathy and neuropathy
Coordinate care through a specialist metabolic team with dietetic support

Provide genetic counselling for autosomal recessive HADHA inheritance, offer family and newborn screening, and counsel mothers on the risk of acute fatty liver of pregnancy and HELLP when carrying an affected foetus
